$comment: One entry per Pi package. source=npm: packages/<dir> holds the exact published tarball contents. source=git: packages/<dir> holds the repository contents at the pinned commit. An entry with paths holds only those paths. Local changes to upstream packages live in patches/<dir>/*.patch. source=own: our own package, its code edited in packages/<dir> directly. Its entry records its direct dependency pins and either each vendored dependency (direct and transitive) with its version and lockfile integrity, when node_modules is committed (web), or the lockfile as the integrity record, when node_modules is installed by the dotfiles (web-tools).

integrity.contentSha256Method: cd packages/infisical-ai-skills && find . -type f | LC_ALL=C sort | xargs shasum -a 256 | shasum -a 256 (LC_ALL=C: the order of sort, and so the hash, otherwise depends on the locale; contentSha256: upstream paths before patches; patchedContentSha256: after patches, what packages/ holds)

patches.reason: Upstream infisical-setup description is 1188 characters; Pi caps descriptions at 1024 and warns at startup. Drops the SDK and auth-method enumerations (still listed in references/sdks.md and references/machine-identity-auth.md) and shortens the 'Use' clause, to 1020 characters.

infisical-ai-skills.review: Markdown only (17 files: 3 SKILL.md, 13 references, LICENSE): no scripts, no executable files. Commands quoted are the official CLI installers (artifacts-cli.infisical.com, curl|bash in Docker/CI examples), `npx skills add`, `pip install infisicalsdk`; some lines still cite dl.cloudsmith.io, retired on 2026-09-16. No hidden instructions found. Our rules live in pi-agent skills/infisical, which takes precedence.

integrity.contentSha256Method: cd packages/emilkowalski-skills && find . -type f | LC_ALL=C sort | xargs shasum -a 256 | shasum -a 256 (LC_ALL=C: the order of sort, and so the hash, otherwise depends on the locale)

emilkowalski-skills.review: Markdown only (18 SKILL.md, 8 companion files next to them, LICENSE): no scripts, no executable files. Reviewed by scanning every file for shell commands, URLs, HTML comments and invisible characters, and by reading each frontmatter; the bodies were not read line by line. No install or network command is given to the agent; the skills tell it to edit the project's code, and learn-taste to write the user's design corrections into the project's DESIGN.md, a project skill or a lint check. URLs are documentation links (library sites, emilkowal.ski, easing tools). Zero-width spaces in improve-animations/PLAN-TEMPLATE.md only escape nested code fences. Left out: animate-expo (React Native and Expo) and write-swift (Swift), not web front end; ask-emil, animate, animation-performance and mobile-native still name them. ask-emil, learn-taste, pick-ui-library, prototype and review-animations set disable-model-invocation: they load only when called by name. harness check.sh reports those five descriptions without a 'Use when' and emil-design-eng's body over 500 lines (680): upstream style, kept.

web.review: Licenses: MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, Apache-2.0. No install script (prepare scripts only, which a registry install never runs; installed with --ignore-scripts). No network or process access in the code that loads: domutils' fetch() is a local feed helper; linkedom's ./worker export, domino's .yarn and test files are never imported. unpdf 2.2.2 (2.2.3, published that day, was inside pnpm's minimumReleaseAge, for which pnpm wrote itself an exclusion; not taken) bundles a serverless pdf.js (1.7 MB, plus image decoders loaded only by registerImageDecoders): no eval and no Function constructor in the bundle, so there is no isEvalSupported to turn off; its 'workers' are in-process WorkerTasks; fetch and fs are used only for a document, font or CMap given by URL, and with no pdfjs-dist installed unpdf sets no font or CMap URL. gitleaks with .gitleaks.toml on node_modules (copied under another name, since the default rules skip node_modules): no finding.

web-tools.node_modules: not committed: the dotfiles install it from the frozen lockfile; pnpm-lock.yaml is the integrity record of the whole tree
web-tools.review: Tree: 50 packages, licenses Apache-2.0, MIT, ISC, (AFL-2.1 OR BSD-3-Clause); no install, preinstall or postinstall script (chrome-devtools-mcp has a prepare script, which a registry install never runs); pnpm reports no build script awaiting approval. Agent skills offered by e2e and chrome-devtools-mcp are denied in pnpm-workspace.yaml (the e2e skill is vendored and reviewed in packages/e2e). Network calls made by themselves: e2e telemetry to eu.i.posthog.com and its npm latest-version check (only on a terminal), both off with E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 in mcp.json; chrome-devtools-mcp usage statistics (play.googleapis.com/log) off with --no-usage-statistics, CrUX lookups (chromeuxreport.googleapis.com) off with --no-performance-crux, and its daily npm latest-version check off with CHROME_DEVTOOLS_MCP_NO_UPDATE_CHECKS=1 in mcp.json; browsers are downloaded only by e2e-web install. Files written outside the run directory: e2e its preferences under ~/.config/e2e, Playwright its browsers under ~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright; chrome-devtools-mcp ~/.cache/chrome-devtools-mcp only for its update check and for a profile when it launches a browser itself, which our launcher never makes it do (--browserUrl).

e2e.review: Markdown only (SKILL.md and its 8 references), plus the LICENSE and the NOTICE, which Apache-2.0 requires to travel with a redistribution: no scripts, no executable files. Tarball sha512 equals npm's dist.integrity and the e2e integrity in packages/web-tools/pnpm-lock.yaml: the skill documents the pinned binary. The skill tells the agent to run npx e2e (guide, run, list, explore, doctor, cache, models, mcp, telemetry), also as pnpm exec e2e or bunx e2e; npx e2e upgrade and npx e2e@latest upgrade (e2e, its @e2e-dev packages and the skill's copies); e2e init, also as pnpm dlx e2e init and npx e2e@latest init (writes into a project a config, an example test, dependencies and a script in package.json, .gitignore, the skill under .agents/skills and .claude/skills with a line in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, the MCP server in .mcp.json, .cursor/mcp.json and .codex/config.toml, and a CI workflow with --ci); claude mcp add --scope project (registers the MCP server in a project); npm install --save-dev e2e @e2e-dev/web ai; npx @e2e-dev/web install or e2e-web install (downloads browsers, and system libraries on Linux with --with-deps); npx e2e login <provider> (model OAuth saved under ~/.config/e2e); npx on packages that are not in our pinned tree, so fetched from npm when run: unbox-ai (reads an AI trace), agent-device (mobile devices), vercel link, create-next-app; gh issue list -R e2e-inc/e2e; engine sessions without a config; a bug bash (parallel e2e explore jobs; writes a bug-bash config, a seed script, repro tests and .e2e/bugbash into a project); and npx e2e feedback (sends a report to e2e's team, after --dry-run and the user's consent). It documents E2E_TELEMETRY_DISABLED. Our rules live in pi-agent skills/web, which takes precedence. Description 681 characters, name e2e: no patch. harness check.sh reports references/explore.md (142 lines) without a Contents heading: upstream style, kept.
